neighbours.label: Elements and gases that emit, in atomic spectra and chemistry (hydrogen emits spectral lines, sulfur oxides, sodium, an atom shifting color); sound and motion in the same frames stay quiet
fire: When neon gas is excited, it gives off bright spectral lines.
Heated helium produces an emission spectrum of narrow lines.
The furnace releases nitrogen oxides and carbon monoxide.
An excited atom drops to a lower level and emits a photon.
Volcanic gases contain sulfur dioxide, chlorine and water vapour.
Each element has its own characteristic absorption lines.
The comet's tail shows sodium, potassium and cyanide.
A star's light reveals hydrogen and calcium lines.
quiet: When the door is opened, it gives off a long creak.
Heated soup produces a pleasant smell of onions in the hall.
The furnace warms the kitchen and the small bedroom.
A tired runner drops to a lower pace and takes a drink.
School bags contain books, pencils and a packed lunch.
Each family has its own favourite holiday songs.
The parade's end shows dancers, drummers and clowns.
A star's fan club holds parties and dinners.

notes: Probes: spectral ' lines' 0.80, 'ides' of oxides 0.35, others about 0.20. ASCII and ANSI code examples are not covered.
